subject: math
title: Grade 7 Circumference and Area of Circles
seo_title: Grade 7 Circumference and Area of Circles Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 math worksheets on circumference and area of circles for the BC curriculum: radius and diameter, C = πd = 2πr, A = πr² and finding the diameter from the circumference, with bike wheel, table and garden problems. 100 questions with an answer key, good FSA numeracy practice.
key_big: Circumference C = πd = 2πr. Area A = πr². Use π ≈ 3.14.
key_sub: The diameter is 2 radii, so halve d before you use A = πr². Square only r, not π. C is a length (cm); A is in square units (cm²).
body_html:
Parts of a circle

The centre is the middle point. A radius (r) goes from the centre to the edge. A diameter (d) goes all the way across through the centre. The circumference (C) is the distance all the way around: the perimeter of the circle.

Circumference: C = πd = 2πr

For every circle, C ÷ d is the same number. It is called π (pi). π = 3.14159…, and in these worksheets we use π ≈ 3.14. So the circumference is a little more than 3 diameters.

Example 1

A bike wheel has a diameter of 60 cm. How far does it roll in one turn?

C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 60 = 188.4

Answer: 188.4 cm

Example 2

A circle has a radius of 5 m. Find its circumference.

d = 2 × 5 = 10 m. C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 10 = 31.4

Answer: 31.4 m

Area: A = πr²

Square the radius, then multiply by π. The circle covers about 3.14 squares of side r. Area is in square units, such as cm² or m².

Example 3

A round table has a diameter of 2 m. Find the area of its top.

r = 2 ÷ 2 = 1 m. A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 1 × 1 = 3.14

Answer: 3.14 m²

Working backwards

If you know the circumference, divide by π to get the diameter: d = C ÷ π. Then halve it for the radius.

Example 4

A tree trunk is 1.57 m around. Find its diameter.

d = C ÷ π ≈ 1.57 ÷ 3.14 = 0.5

Answer: 0.5 m

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the diameter in A = πr²Halve d first: r = d ÷ 2
C = πrC = 2πr (or C = πd)
Squaring π: (3.14 × 5)²Square only r: 3.14 × 5²
Mixing up C and AC is a length (cm); A is an area (cm²)
Multiplying C by π to find dDivide: d = C ÷ π

faq.q: Do Grade 7 students in BC learn circumference and area of circles?
faq.a: Yes. Circumference and area of circles are part of Geometry and measurement in the BC Grade 7 math curriculum. Students find C = πd and A = πr² and use them to solve problems.

faq.q: What is the difference between circumference and area?
faq.a: Circumference is the distance around a circle, measured in units like cm. Area is the space inside the circle, measured in square units like cm².

faq.q: What value of π should Grade 7 students use?
faq.a: Most Grade 7 work uses π ≈ 3.14, or the π key on a calculator. These worksheets use 3.14 so answers can be checked by hand.

faq.q: Do these circle worksheets help with the Grade 7 FSA?
faq.a: Yes. The Grade 7 FSA includes numeracy, where students solve problems with measurement and decimals. Wheel, table and garden problems like these are good practice.

items.q: What is the red line called?
items.e: It goes from the centre to the edge, so it is a radius.

items.q: The red line goes through the centre. What is it called?
items.e: It goes all the way across the circle through the centre, so it is a diameter.

items.q: What is the red edge of this circle called?
items.e: The distance all the way around a circle is its circumference. It is the perimeter of the circle.

items.q: What is the red point called?
items.e: The point in the middle, the same distance from every point on the edge, is the centre.

items.q: What is the diameter of this circle?
items.e: The diameter is 2 radii: d = 2r = 2 × 6 = 12 cm.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 9 cm. What is its diameter?
items.e: The diameter is 2 radii: d = 2r = 2 × 9 = 18 cm.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 15 m. What is its diameter?
items.e: The diameter is 2 radii: d = 2r = 2 × 15 = 30 m.

items.e: The diameter is 2 radii: d = 2r = 2 × 4.5 = 9 cm.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 12.5 m. What is its diameter?
items.e: The diameter is 2 radii: d = 2r = 2 × 12.5 = 25 m.

items.q: What is the radius of this circle?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: r = d ÷ 2 = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 30 m. What is its radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: r = d ÷ 2 = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 m.

items.e: The radius is half the diameter: r = d ÷ 2 = 9 ÷ 2 = 4.5 cm.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 50 mm. What is its radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: r = d ÷ 2 = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 mm.

items.q: A circle has a diameter of 7.6 cm. What is its radius?
items.e: The radius is half the diameter: r = d ÷ 2 = 7.6 ÷ 2 = 3.8 cm.

items.q: How does the diameter of a circle compare with its radius?
c: It is π times as long
items.e: A diameter is made of two radii end to end, so d = 2r. It is 2 times as long.

items.q: For every circle, the circumference divided by the diameter is the same number. What is it called?
items.e: C ÷ d is always the same for every circle. This number is π, about 3.14.

items.q: About how many diameters fit around the circumference of a circle?
items.e: C = π × d and π ≈ 3.14, so the circumference is a little more than 3 diameters. About 6 is the number of radii that fit around (2π ≈ 6.28).

items.q: A circle has a radius of 5 cm. Which is the longest?
items.e: r = 5 cm, d = 10 cm and C ≈ 3.14 × 10 = 31.4 cm. The circumference is the longest.

items.q: Kai draws a circle with a compass. He opens the compass to 4 cm. What is the diameter of his circle?
items.e: The compass opening is the radius: r = 4 cm. d = 2 × 4 = 8 cm.

items.q: Every radius of the same circle is…
items.e: Every point on the circle is the same distance from the centre, so all radii are the same length.

items.q: Which formula gives the circumference of a circle with diameter d?
items.e: The circumference is π times the diameter: C = πd. πr² is the area.

items.q: Which formula gives the circumference of a circle with radius r?
items.e: d = 2r, so C = πd = π × 2r = 2πr. Do not forget the 2.

items.q: Find the circumference. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 10 = 31.4 cm. Using 2πd would double it.

Circle A has a diameter of 10 cm. Circle B has a radius of 6 cm. Which has the longer circumference?
items.e: Circle B has d = 2 × 6 = 12 cm, which is more than 10 cm. A bigger diameter means a longer circumference: 31.4 cm for A and 37.68 cm for B. Circle B.

items.q: The diameter of a circle doubles from 5 cm to 10 cm. What happens to the circumference?
items.e: C = πd: 3.14 × 5 = 15.7 cm and 3.14 × 10 = 31.4 cm. Double the diameter, and the circumference doubles too.

items.q: Which formula gives the area of a circle?
items.e: A = πr²: square the radius, then multiply by π. Only r is squared, not π.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 3 cm. In which unit is its area measured?
items.e: Area counts squares, so it is in square units: cm². Circumference is a length, in cm.

items.q: A circle has a radius of 5 cm. Find its area. Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 3.14 × 25 = 78.5 cm². Square the radius, not π.

items.e: A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 3 × 3 = 3.14 × 9 = 28.26 m². Square the radius, not π.

sets.title: Finding r or d from the circumference

items.q: You know the circumference of a circle. How do you find its diameter?
items.e: C = πd, so d = C ÷ π. Divide C by π (about 3.14).

items.q: You know the circumference of a circle. How do you find its radius?
items.e: C = 2πr, so r = C ÷ 2π. Divide C by 2π (about 6.28). Dividing by π gives the diameter.

sets.title: Word problems: wheels, tables and gardens

items.q: Liam’s bike wheel has a diameter of 66 cm. How far does the bike move in one full turn of the wheel? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: One turn rolls out the circumference. C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 66 = 207.24 cm.

items.q: The wheel on Liam’s bike goes 207.24 cm in one turn. How many metres does the bike go in 100 turns?
Ava rides her bike 1 km along the Seawall in Stanley Park. Her wheels have a diameter of 64 cm. About how many full turns does each wheel make? (1 km = 100 000 cm) Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 64 = 200.96 cm. 100 000 ÷ 200.96 ≈ 497.6, so about 498 turns. Dividing by 64 forgets π.

items.q: A round table in the library is 1.2 m across. What is the area of the tabletop, to the nearest hundredth? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: 1.2 m across is the diameter, so r = 0.6 m. A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 0.36 = 1.1304 ≈ 1.13 m².

items.q: Simran glues ribbon around the edge of a round table with a diameter of 1.2 m. How much ribbon does she need, to the nearest tenth of a metre? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: The edge is the circumference. C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 1.2 = 3.768 ≈ 3.8 m.

items.q: A circular garden in Kelowna has a radius of 3 m. How long is a fence that goes all the way around it? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: The fence is the circumference. d = 6 m, so C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 6 = 18.84 m.

items.q: The same circular garden has a radius of 3 m. What area does it cover? Use π ≈ 3.14.
Mateo puts a fence around a circular garden with a radius of 2 m. The fencing costs $12 per metre. How much does the fencing cost? Use π ≈ 3.14.
A circular flower bed has a diameter of 8 m. One bag of mulch covers 5 m². How many bags does Jasleen need to cover the whole bed? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: r = 4 m. A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 16 = 50.24 m². 50.24 ÷ 5 = 10.048, so 10 bags are not quite enough. She needs 11 bags.

items.q: Owen wraps a rope around a cedar trunk in Pacific Spirit Park. The rope measures 4.71 m. What is the diameter of the trunk? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: The rope measures the circumference. d = C ÷ π ≈ 4.71 ÷ 3.14 = 1.5 m.

items.q: A lawn sprinkler waters a circle with a radius of 5 m. What area of grass does it water? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 25 = 78.5 m². 31.4 is the circumference, not the area.

items.q: A round trampoline has a diameter of 3.6 m. A safety net goes all the way around the edge. How long is the net, to the nearest tenth of a metre? Use π ≈ 3.14.
Which gives more pizza: one round pizza 30 cm across, or two round pizzas 20 cm across? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: 30 cm pizza: r = 15, A ≈ 3.14 × 225 = 706.5 cm². Two 20 cm pizzas: r = 10, A ≈ 2 × 314 = 628 cm². So one 30 cm pizza gives more, even though 20 + 20 > 30.

items.q: A circular path around a pond in a Surrey park has a radius of 50 m. Mei walks around it 3 times. How far does she walk? Use π ≈ 3.14.
The classroom clock has a round face with a radius of 15 cm. What is the area of the clock face? Use π ≈ 3.14.
The edge of a round tree stump measures 2.512 m around. What is the radius of the stump? Use π ≈ 3.14.
A circle painted on a hockey rink has a radius of 4.5 m. How long is the painted line around it? Use π ≈ 3.14.
Harjot’s hand drum has a round top 40 cm across. What is the area of the drum’s top? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: 40 cm across is the diameter, so r = 20 cm. A = πr² ≈ 3.14 × 400 = 1256 cm².

items.q: Which is longer: the circumference of a circle with a diameter of 10 cm, or the perimeter of a square with 8 cm sides? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: Circle: C ≈ 3.14 × 10 = 31.4 cm. Square: P = 4 × 8 = 32 cm. The square’s perimeter is longer by 0.6 cm.

items.q: A Ferris wheel at a summer fair in Abbotsford has a diameter of 20 m. How far does a seat travel in one full turn? Use π ≈ 3.14.
items.e: The seat travels the circumference. C = πd ≈ 3.14 × 20 = 62.8 m.
